The method name 'test7' is generic and does not follow a descriptive naming convention (methodName_scenario_expectedResult). It does not convey the scenario or expected outcome.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The class imports EvoSuite runtime and uses EvoRunner and EvoRunnerParameters and a generic test name ('test7'), indicating heavy use of a test-generation tool and auto-generated naming patterns.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The class-level Javadoc asserts a Given-When-Then structure and the test demonstrates a focused scenario, indicating some upfront design intent and prioritization.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test exercises public API methods only (constructor, insereAresta, grafoTransposto, existeAresta, numVertices) and does not access private state or use reflection, so it focuses on observable behavior.

The test uses specific assertions (assertFalse, assertEquals) rather than generic assertTrue, and verifies multiple concrete properties. Although assertions lack custom messages, they are specific and clear.
The class-level Javadoc is informative; there are no excessive inline comments or commented-out code within the method. Comments present explain intent rather than restating obvious code.
No sources of non-determinism (random, time-based calls, Thread.sleep) are used in the method. The method uses deterministic inputs and local state only.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only creates in-memory objects and uses local variables; it does not persist files, modify static state, or perform operations that require cleanup.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing meaningful classification for selective execution.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single requirement/behavior with one clear Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make failures easy to diagnose. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if exactly one method call / scenario is tested. DECISION RULES: 1) Count distinct Act operations: this method invokes insereAresta, grafoTransposto and existeAresta; multiple method calls related to different logical steps are present. 2) No name suggests multiple operations. 3) Because there are multiple distinct operations contributing to the asserted outcomes, mark as non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on each other and should run independently. RATIONALE: Independence enables flexible execution order. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for @Before/@After or shared mutable state. DECISION RULES: No @Before/@After present in the snippet, and the method uses only local variables; no static/instance shared state is visible. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should cover both happy paths and error conditions. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for exception tests or explicitly invalid inputs. DECISION RULES: Only one test is present and it exercises a happy path; there are no tests checking invalid inputs or exceptions (no assertThrows/@Test(expected=...) visible). VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate boundary values (zero, negative, max). RATIONALE: Boundaries are common failure points. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for 0, -1, empty, max values. DECISION RULES: The test uses vertex index 0 (a boundary value) and constructs a graph with a specific size; presence of 0 indicates some boundary coverage. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helpers to remove duplication. RATIONALE: Improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for helper methods/constants or short non-duplicated tests. DECISION RULES: The test is short, self-contained (<10 lines) and does not show duplicated logic across methods in the provided snippet; thus acceptable. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and with low cyclomatic complexity. RATIONALE: Easier to reason about. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Count lines, loops, conditionals. DECISION RULES: This method is short (<20 lines) with linear flow and no loops/branches. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should comprehensively verify results. RATIONALE: More assertions increase fault detection. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Check number and richness of assertions. DECISION RULES: The test verifies vertex counts for both graphs and the existence of the transposed edge (multiple properties). VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out tests. RATIONALE: Ignored tests provide no value. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test. DECISION RULES: No such annotations or commented-out tests are visible in the snippet. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should reference requirements/ticket IDs. RATIONALE: Enables traceability to requirements. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for annotations or Javadoc referencing IDs. DECISION RULES: Class-level Javadoc includes 'REQ-GRAFO-001', providing direct requirement traceability. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests should be separate and explicit. RATIONALE: Non-functional tests require dedicated tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for timing annotations or security assertions. DECISION RULES: Unit test shown is functional and contains no performance/security-specific tests; performance/security is typically not applicable for this unit test. VERDICT: not-applicable.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome. RATIONALE: Descriptive names are self-documenting. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Check method name patterns like method_condition_result. DECISION RULES: Method name is 'test5' (generic) and does not describe behavior or expected result. Despite class-level Javadoc, the method name itself is not descriptive. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Generated tests should be minimal and intention-revealing. RATIONALE: Auto-generated verbose tests are hard to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for auto-generated names and EvoSuite artifacts. DECISION RULES: Presence of EvoRunner, EvoRunnerParameters, EvoAssertions imports and a generic method name 'test5' are signals of heavy test generation. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show design intent (Given-When-Then, BDD). RATIONALE: Thoughtful test design encourages thorough coverage. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for Given-When-Then comments or BDD naming and coverage of scenarios. DECISION RULES: The class-level Javadoc claims Given-When-Then, but the test method itself lacks explicit Given-When-Then structure and there is only a single basic happy-path test; no edge or error scenarios are provided. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should target public behavior instead of implementation details. RATIONALE: Reduces brittleness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for reflection or internal state access. DECISION RULES: The test uses public Grafo methods (constructor, insereAresta, grafoTransposto, existeAresta, numVertices) and does not access private internals or reflection. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be specific and informative. RATIONALE: Specific assertions detect subtle faults. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Prefer assertEquals/assertThat over generic assertTrue; presence of messages helps. DECISION RULES: The test uses specific assertions (assertEquals for counts) and assertTrue for edge existence; while no custom messages are used, assertions are specific and validate multiple properties. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain why, not what; code should be readable. RATIONALE: Avoid excessive or misleading comments. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for commented-out code or excessive comments. DECISION RULES: The class provides useful Javadoc and there is no commented-out code in the test method. Comments are not excessive. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should avoid non-deterministic sources. RATIONALE: Flaky tests erode confidence. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for Random, current time, sleeps, external dependencies. DECISION RULES: The method contains no Random, time-based calls, sleeps, or external calls; uses local deterministic operations. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should not leave persistent side effects or modify global state. RATIONALE: Prevents inter-test interference. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for file/database creation, static modifications, or missing cleanup. DECISION RULES: This test uses local objects only and does not persist data or modify static fields; no cleanup is required. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use tags/categories to organize tests. RATIONALE: Enables selective execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for @Tag/@Category annotations. DECISION RULES: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class) at class level, providing categorization. VERDICT: compliant.
